extraction.name: ChartQA
extraction.description: A large-scale benchmark for question answering about charts that covers 9.6K human-written questions as well as 23.1K questions generated from human-written chart summaries, focusing on visual and logical reasoning questions over real-world charts.
extraction.creator: Ahmed Masry, Do Xuan Long, Jia Qing Tan, Shafiq Joty, Enamul Hoque
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Charts were crawled from four online platforms: Statista, Pew Research, Our World In Data (OWID), and OECD. For Pew, only chart images were collected because underlying data tables were unavailable. For Statista, OWID, and OECD, underlying data tables, metadata (title, chart type), SVG files, and associated text descriptions were extracted along with bounding boxes from the SVG files.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: For the Pew dataset, only chart images were crawled because the underlying data tables are not available.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Statista (statista.com), Pew Research (pewresearch.org), Our World In Data (ourworldindata.org), and Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (oecd.org).
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: For machine-generated questions, a heuristic was applied to filter out invalid/unanswerable questions if the answer could not be found in the chart data table. The test set of the machine-generated dataset was also manually cleaned by removing invalid questions. For modeling, data tables were flattened and concatenated with question tokens.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Two annotation procedures were conducted: (1) Human-authored QA collection via Amazon Mechanical Turk, where crowdworkers provided two questions (compositional or visual) and answers per chart, which were verified by a second annotator; mismatches were manually checked. (2) Automatic question generation using two fine-tuned T5 models (one for answer extraction and one for question generation) applied to human-written Statista chart summaries.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Agreement between crowdworkers based on exact match was 61.04%. When manually checking agreement on 500 random samples accounting for typos and lexical variations, agreement was 78.55%. For machine-generated questions, manual analysis of 1,250 QA pairs showed 86.64% were complete, answerable, and correct.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Amazon Mechanical Turk workers were required to have an acceptance rate of 95% and at least 5,000 approved HITs, and passed a qualification pre-test. They were compensated $0.60 USD per 3-5 minute task based on the US minimum wage of $7.25/hour. All annotations were anonymized.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: Models trained on this dataset can potentially be abused to mislead the public regarding chart content and implications. The models are not guaranteed to produce correct outputs at all times.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Topic distribution has an overrepresentation of politics, particularly in the Pew dataset where 45.4% of charts relate to U.S. Politics & Policy. Bar charts are also heavily represented compared to line and pie charts.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Existing models struggle with complex nested operations, error propagation when chart tables must be extracted automatically from diverse visual styles, and representations that fail to fully capture the relations between visual marks and underlying data tables.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, validation, and benchmarking of visual question answering and chart reasoning models.
